clue.text: Hunting for Hollywood's benevolence

definitions.meaning: the 1997 Hollywood film is ... Hunting, so these words come before 'Hunting' in its title
kindly feeling or friendly disposition towards others

explanation.surface: A film fan looks for kindness in the movie business.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a fill-in-the-blank: Good Will Hunting is the Hollywood film starring Matt Damon.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is a friendly, kindly attitude, a close synonym for benevolence.

clue.text: Guy from Scotland's heading to place on river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so the S comes first
the heading of a word is its first letter, here the start of Scotland's

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: A Scottish man heads off to settle beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; here it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a supporting rope or wire, and a stay is the nautical term for the same kind of brace.

clue.text: One finding model on horse?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece placed on the second sits above it

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
a racer is a racehorse

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fashion model sitting on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is a person or device that tracks down lost things, such as a tracer of missing goods.

clue.text: Reference book with one page on a currency conflict arising in Greece

definitions.note: the definition is the adjective in the phrase Oedipal conflict, the psychological struggle named from the Theban king

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the later ones

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
the Roman numeral for one
L stands for the lira or the pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry on a currency dispute that broke out in Greece, recalling the euro crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'currency conflict arising in Greece' suggests the euro crisis, but the conflict is Freud's, named for a Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's Oedipus complex, the son's rivalry with his father, takes its name from the Greek myth of Oedipus of Thebes.

clue.text: Number of letters from one pen — thence….

indicators.note: letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer's letters drawn from a single pen, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this was a drug that dulled grief and pain, so it is literally a thing that numbs.

clue.text: …..cheap claim, one about housing company

indicators.note: housing means the shuffled letters hold the company abbreviation inside them
about here means turned around, so the letters of claim and one are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue, a cheap claim made by someone about a firm sheltering it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this clue to the one before, but each stands alone; 'about' here is the anagram signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means sparing with money or giving good value, so it can stand for inexpensive.

clue.text: Pass on setter's role

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, and setter's means I am, written I'M
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: The setter describes handing over their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge or news is to hand it on to someone else.

clue.text: Name given to counter-revolutionary piece

indicators.note: the abbreviation is handed to, so set before, the following letters
revolutionary means turning over, so the letters of counter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A title is bestowed on an anti-revolution work of art or tract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-revolutionary' looks like one political word; it splits into the fodder and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a short, dreamy musical composition, so it is a piece in the musical sense.

clue.text: Pitch tents in interior part of Kenya, about to assume missionary position initially

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the letters for about take on the initials that follow
only an inner stretch of the word Kenya is kept, its outer letters and one inner letter being dropped

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: In the Kenyan interior, someone is about to take up a post as a missionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior part of' keeps only EN from inside Kenya. 'missionary position' invites a smirk, but it only supplies two initials, M and P.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp, which means putting up tents.

clue.text: Regulars in wind play in a lazy way

indicators.note: regulars are letters taken at regular intervals, here every second one of the two words

explanation.surface: Regular players of wind instruments perform without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulars' looks like a band's members, but it picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idly means without effort or purpose, which is how a lazy person does things.

clue.text: Conflict arising from 15 act by Egyptian leader (Christian)

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces go next to each other

parts.note: the answer to 15 across means wrong or unlawful, and an unlawful act is a crime
Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt from 1970 to 1981

explanation.surface: A war sparked by a crime committed by an Egyptian ruler, with a Christian aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'Christian' pairs with '(Muslim)' in the next clue: the 1853-56 war pitted Christian powers and the Muslim Ottoman Empire, and began over Christian access to holy places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853-56 was fought by Britain, France and Turkey against Russia, a famous nineteenth-century conflict.

clue.text: Current with origin in Zambia, described by 4 foreign official (Muslim)

indicators.note: described means drawn around, so the German number goes around the other letters

parts.note: four in German is vier, so the number 4 in a foreign language
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: a word's origin is its first letter

explanation.surface: A foreign official is described by flow and beginnings in Zambia, an African setting.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 down, but it is the number itself, in German.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high-ranking minister in Muslim states such as the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Not clear it's wrong going topless once soft bit of porn's not 15

indicators.note: losing the top letter, which in a down clue is the first

parts.note: a sin is something that is wrong
ex means former, once
p means soft (piano) in music, and it is also the first bit of porn
15 across is unlawful, and the opposite of unlawful is licit

explanation.surface: A prudish complaint that topless photos and soft porn are wrong and not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the first letter of SIN, leaving IN. LICIT, meaning lawful, is the opposite of 15 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexplicit is not stated plainly, so its meaning is not clear.

clue.text: Take the manual out of car going to China

indicators.note: going to joins the second piece on after the first

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone ships a car with manual gears off to China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To automate a process is to make machines do it, removing the manual work from it.

clue.text: Wrong number secured by setter on adult line

indicators.note: the number is fastened onto the setter, so it follows straight after

parts.note: the setter calls themself I
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
A is the old film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A wrong telephone number is kept by the setter on a line for grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also the on side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means against the law, so it describes something wrong.

clue.text: Bird life by Victoria Falls unlikely all to be greatly reduced in two separate areas

indicators.note: in means the cut-down words are put inside the pair of area letters

parts.note: a is the abbreviation for area, and two separate ones go one each side
the second area abbreviation, on the other side
Victoria greatly reduced to its first two letters
Falls greatly reduced to its first two letters
unlikely greatly reduced to its first two letters

explanation.surface: Birds near Victoria Falls are unlikely all to be badly hit in two different regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all to be greatly reduced' tells you to cut each of Victoria, Falls and unlikely to two letters, giving VIFAUN, which sits between two A's for area.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective name for the birds of a region, its bird population.

clue.text: Following storm, upset about a little crack in these?

definitions.text: Following storm, upset about a little crack in these?

indicators.note: to storm is to rage wildly, so the letters following it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: After a fuss over a small breakage, the crockery is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'a storm in a teacup', a great fuss over a trifle. 'storm' rearranges UPSET with C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Small china cups for tea are where the proverbial storm happens, and they can have a little crack.

clue.text: Complaint from Ugandan leader in reply is outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous means wild, so the letters are mixed up
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An African leader's answer is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance; here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleurisy is inflammation of the lining of the lungs, and a complaint can mean an ailment.

clue.text: Confessed in front of seedy hotel by 24D, say, almost at its source

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces go next to each other
the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 24 down is an example of a river
the source of the river at 24 down is its first letter, N

explanation.surface: A confession made outside a sleazy hotel beside the Nile, near where it rises.
explanation.walkthrough: '24D, say' points to NILE as an example of a RIVER, cut to RIVE by 'almost'; the Nile's source gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shriven is to have confessed to a priest and received absolution.

clue.text: Buxom topless female is hot swimmer

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter is removed

parts.note: plump means full-figured, buxom
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A curvy woman with no top on is very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' looks like a person in the pool; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The lumpfish is a lumpy North Atlantic fish, and a swimmer is a crossword term for any fish.

clue.text: Organ used by Erasure turns up

used by says the letters are taken from inside the following words

clue.text: Environment of place beyond Malawi when a law's ignored

indicators.note: the place comes beyond, so after, the first piece
ignored means these letters are left out of the country's name

parts.note: the words a law, spelt out, with the 's meaning is
lieu is French for place, as in the phrase in lieu of

explanation.surface: Somewhere past Malawi where the law is disregarded.

clue.text: Bold complaint of wimpy male that's turned tail

indicators.note: the tail end of the phrase is turned around, so its last two letters swap

parts.note: man flu is the jokey name for a mild cold that a man treats as serious illness

explanation.walkthrough: 'turned tail' looks like fleeing, but it swaps the last two letters, making LU into UL.
explanation.definitionFit: Manful means brave and resolute, so it is a synonym of bold.

clue.text: Erotic anti-war poetry reading?

indicators.note: war is a fight, so the letters before it are battled into a new order

explanation.surface: A recital of sexy pacifist verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-war' looks like one word but splits: the anagram signal is 'war'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitation is a spoken performance of a poem from memory.

clue.text: Standard choice of letters to be typed in line with CV

definitions.meaning: a usual level or expected pattern

definitions.text: choice of letters to be typed in line with CV
definitions.meaning: on a keyboard's bottom row the keys after C and V include N and M

explanation.walkthrough: On a QWERTY keyboard the bottom row runs Z X C V B N M; 'N or M' offers a choice of two letters on that row.

clue.text: Smelly fruit from Italy eaten by half of 80s pop group

clue.text: Make uniform for one in a sequel that's been cast

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
